frequency_question: How often does an administrative agency successfully complete the formal revocation of an established accreditor's authority within a short statutory window despite procedural friction?
membership_rule: Includes formal Department-level proceedings aimed at stripping national or professional accrediting agencies of federal recognition; excludes voluntary relinquishments or minor sanctions falling short of full revocation.

cases.name: American Bar Association accreditation review (historical challenge 1)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) termination round 1

coverage_note: 3 major contested revocation proceedings identified in the modern administrative era; 2 resulted in eventual termination, but none successfully traversed the full administrative due process lifecycle within a 92-day window.
known_gaps: Lower-profile advisory committee recommendations that were resolved informally without reaching a formal final secretary order.
skeleton: Total historical federal attempts to strip major institutional/professional accreditors of recognition since 1994, decomposed into completed revocations versus successful defenses or prolonged procedural appeals.
multiplier: 2 successful revocations / 3 major contested termination proceedings = 66.6% base success rate for initiated actions, but filtering for completion strictly within a compressed 92-day window yields near zero due to mandatory notice, comment periods, and administrative hearings.
validity_reason: Administrative procedures act requirements and Department of Education recognition regulations change slowly via negotiated rulemaking cycles.
